# Locale text collation native observations

text collation non-English SOQL text collation capture (follow-up to text collation)
org: fresh scratch org from a campaign Dev Hub, 30-day, Developer Edition (OrganizationType "Developer Edition", IsSandbox true); created 2026-11-13T03:44:44Z (host clock), deleted 2026-11-13T04:13:09Z; delete returned status 0 and a later org display returned not found. Org id, user ids, usernames, alias and instance host are not recorded.
org locale: Organization.LanguageLocaleKey en_US, DefaultLocaleSidKey en_US. Running user (anonymous default) LocaleSidKey en_US, LanguageLocaleKey en_US.
tooling: sf 2.157.8; scratch HOME with SF_USE_GENERIC_UNIX_KEYCHAIN=true. Direct sf driver, not capture.sh (the 4000 character test-message cap needed chunking). Packet: the accompanying sources/ (gen-packet.py generates it; maps/V-values.tsv decodes labels; specs.json lists the strings).
API versions: 62.0 and 67.0 (class apiVersion matches the --api-version of the anonymous run). Every (locale, API) cell was run once. 62.0 and 67.0 agree in all 106 locales (0 differences between the two APIs after the identical probe).
mechanics: 760 distinct strings (shuffled, seed 4661; label = index in two base-36 chars) are inserted as Account.Name, label in BillingCity. Probe returns SELECT BillingCity ... ORDER BY Name ASC, BillingCity ASC (ties fall back to label order; BillingCity is plain lowercase base-36 so its own collation is label order), GROUP BY Name with counts, 51 equality probes (Name = :x), 8 range probes (> < >= against single characters z, a, ae-umlaut, b, Z, A, katakana A, n-tilde), MIN/MAX. Strings: ASCII punctuation, digits, Latin letters in both cases, ~230 accented/ligature/digraph forms and names, French secondary pairs, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari, hiragana, katakana, half/full width, ~150 Han, Hangul, emoji, NBSP. Combining-mark sequences included.
route: @IsTest only; per locale a Standard User (LanguageLocaleKey en_US, LocaleSidKey = the locale under test) is created and System.runAs runs the probe. Because the Salesforce message cap is 4000 characters, each locale is three test methods (chunks 0-2 of the same result string); the three chunks are concatenated by the harvest script. Group-by representative labels can differ between the chunk runs (the representative of a case-tie group is not fixed), so only group counts are used.
anonymous check: the running user's LocaleSidKey was set to de_DE, sv_SE, ja_JP and zh_CN in turn (sf data update record), the anonymous probe run at 62.0 and 67.0, then the user restored to en_US. All 8 anonymous cells equal the @IsTest cell for the same locale on asc order, group list, equality probes (test:false vs test:true is the only difference). So anonymous and @IsTest agree; the user LocaleSidKey drives collation, and LanguageLocaleKey does not (text collation T8: de_DE/en_US sorts as de, en_US/de sorts as en_US).
TSV: org.tsv, 224 rows: per API 1 facts row, 1 anonymous default-user row, 4 anonymous user-locale rows (de_DE, sv_SE, ja_JP, zh_CN), plus 106 istest locale rows (ids loc-test-<locale>-<api>). Observation fields: asc = labels in ORDER BY order (comma separated here; the raw capture concatenated them), group = label[xN] list, eq = probe label=matching labels separated by ';', gtz lta gea ltb gtZ ltA gtKa ltn = labels returned by the range probes, min/max labels. Rows with ERR: are invalid LocaleSidKey values (restricted picklist) and are answers.
invalid LocaleSidKey (restricted picklist rejects): he_IL (use iw_IL), id_ID (use in_ID), nb_NO, nn_NO (use no_NO), fo_FO, gl_ES, mn_MN, si_LK, es_ES_TRADITIONAL, ja_JP_TRADITIONAL.

RESULTS (ICU = macOS libicucore 78.1 via ctypes, collator opened with the mapped locale, default attributes; icu-compare.py reproduces):
1. ORDER BY on text is the ICU collator for the user's LocaleSidKey at tertiary strength, default attributes: 79 of 79 locales (106 minus 17 English-like fallback minus 10 invalid) match the ICU tertiary order EXACTLY except lv_LV (7 adjacent violations vs ICU 78: macron vowels, y/ij/yo; older CLDR tailoring in Salesforce) . Group-by class counts equal ICU tertiary classes in all 79 (756 of 760 distinct for most; ja_JP 719 and th_TH 717 match ICU tertiary, not quaternary). MIN/MAX equal ICU tertiary first/last in all 79.
2. Default attributes include locale defaults: da_DK and mt_MT uppercase first (caseFirst upper), th_TH alternate shifted (punctuation ignorable), es unaffected (no traditional), fr_CA is NOT backwards-accent (matches fr/root, ICU fr_CA does not), de/it/nl/pt/fr/ca/eu/ga/hy/ka/lb/ms/sw/in_ID = ICU root. Locale tailoring applies, e.g. sv/fi/da/no/is/et/cs/sk/pl/hu/hr/bs/sr/sl/ro/lt/tr/az/vi/el/ru/uk/be/bg/kk/ar/iw/hi/bn/ta/te/ur/ko/ja/th.
3. Chinese: zh_CN, zh_TW, zh_HK, zh_SG, zh_MO = ICU collation=unihan (radical-stroke); zh_CN_PINYIN = pinyin; zh_CN_STROKE, zh_HK_STROKE, zh_TW_STROKE = stroke. Plain zh_CN is NOT pinyin. Japanese = ICU ja (standard). Korean = ICU ko. sr_RS/sr_BA = ICU sr (Cyrillic); sh_BA = sr_Latn=bs=hr on this set (indistinguishable); bs_BA = bs.
4. English-like fallback: en_US, en_GB, en_AU, en_CA, en_IN and af_ZA, cy_GB, fa_IR, kl_GL, km_KH, lo_LA, mk_MK, my_MM, ne_NP, ps_AF, sq_AL, tl_PH give byte-identical orders to en_US (the text collation table: ASCII fixed weights, case-insensitive; code point order above z; 724 groups) and not ICU (114 violations vs ICU root). Salesforce has no ICU path for these; they must stay on the en comparator.
5. Relational comparison in WHERE (> < >= <=) uses the SAME locale collator at SECONDARY strength: 79 of 79 locale cells match the ICU secondary relation on all 8 range probes; primary and tertiary each fail all 79. Visible effect: Name > 'z' excludes 'Z'; Name < 'A' excludes 'a' and fullwidth 'a'; Name > katakana A excludes halfwidth. So ORDER BY ties (tertiary) differ from relational equivalence (secondary).
6. Equality (Name = :x) is not ICU strength-based and is locale-sensitive: 1774 of 1785 probe cells (35 first-batch locales x 51 probes) equal Python str.upper() equivalence (a=A not ae-ordinal or fullwidth, ss=sharp s, dotless i with I, cote=Cote); the 11 differences are locale effects: tr_TR i=dotted capital I and I=dotless i only, el_GR alpha also matches alpha-tonos, zh_CN/zh_TW/ja_JP/ko_KR a/A also match fullwidth A/a. Looks like locale-aware upper-casing; not modeled further (out of scope for ORDER BY).

x/text comparison (golang.org/x/text v0.43.0 as in glade go.mod; collate tables Unicode 6.2.0, CLDR 23; xtext-compare.go.txt is the driver, default collate.New(tag) options, no Loose/IgnoreCase):
- exact (0 adjacent violations vs Salesforce): root/und, de, fr (incl fr_CA, since Salesforce is not backwards), es, it, nl, pt, sv, cs, sk, pl, ro, sl, lt, is, tr, vi, ca, eu, ga, hy, ka, lb, ms, sw, id.
- 1-3 violations: ar, he, hi, bn, ta, te, ur, el, ru, uk, be, bg, kk, sr, hr, ko (non-Latin scripts sort before Latin in Salesforce/ICU via script reordering; x/text CLDR 23 lacks [reorder]), fi (1), hu (1), et (1), az (2), lv (3), zh pinyin (2), zh stroke (1).
- larger: bs/sh digraphs 7, ja 4, nb/no 11 (CLDR tailoring changed after 23), th 22 (no alternate=shifted tailoring), zh unihan 44 (x/text has no unihan; falls back to pinyin), da 112 and mt 109 (caseFirst upper not available in x/text), en and the en-like fallback set 113-118 (use the text collation comparator, not x/text).
- x/text has no caseFirst, no script reorder, no CLDR newer than 23.
non-claims: nothing about SOSL, LIKE, text areas, picklists, custom fields (text collation found Name, custom Text and Contact LastName agree for en_US only), formula or other object fields, or the exact CLDR/ICU version Salesforce runs. Strings outside the set (long names, rare scripts) are untested.

Fixture bytes: org.tsv SHA-256 e26e6c218c2157107e87c95d8120b81a5e0b9b8d7856aa6a38c826759d327aaa; maps/V-values.tsv SHA-256 2376155dff856228dad0fe174fa389c7177ae30a0e1b1f2b353e958b36a8dd26. The observation and map bytes are unchanged from the supplied capture. No new Salesforce run was performed. The 20 invalid-locale answers and two facts rows are retained and accounted separately from 202 comparator observations. Group representatives and MIN/MAX secondary ties are compared by their equivalence classes, not by an unproven representative spelling.

Equality carry: equality-baseline.tsv pins the unchanged local equals behavior by locale before introducing locale collators. The native I/i and ss/sharp-s probes expose existing equality differences. The conformance report separates collation-row matches, native equality matches, and fully native row matches. The equality baseline is a local preservation contract, not a native oracle.
